label: Dividing by a Negative
subgoals: When you divide both sides of an inequality by a negative number, the direction of the inequality reverses.
Check the reversal with a test value.
A common error is to reverse only one side.

label: Solving Step by Step
subgoals: Move constants first so the variable term stands alone.
For -2x + 5 > 11, subtract 5 to get -2x > 6, then divide by -2 to get x < -3.
Write the solution as an inequality and test one number on each side of the boundary.

label: Integer Solutions
subgoals: Word problems often ask for the greatest or least integer that satisfies the inequality.
If x < -3, the greatest integer solution is -4, because -3 itself is excluded.
Sketch the solution on a number line and mark whether the endpoint is filled or open before naming an integer.
